thread:
Kai: quick brain-dump — i'm worried about correctness when we aggressively evict tombstones from the prefix cache. idea: keep a tiny compact 'stale-marker' per-pref (N bytes) for a short window instead of full tombstone. demote path can consult marker to decide read-through vs serve local stale. thoughts? :thinking:

Maya: interesting. what invariants are we targeting? R-A-W per-tenant or causal across cross-shard writes?

Kai: primary goal: per-tenant read-after-write inside a single logical prefix. we currently demote -> remote fetch if prefix absent. if we drop tombstone, concurrent writes might be invisible until remote catches up, leading to stale returns. marker would let demote detect recent mutations without keeping whole KV entry.

Dani: ok but memory/time tradeoff: how many bytes and how long? if marker lifetime is too long we bloat metadata, too short we lose protection. propose: 8-byte compact = epoch (5 bytes) + 3-byte low-entropy checksum, TTL configurable by policy.

Sam: where does the marker live? in slab footer/header or in an adjacent per-prefix metadata slab? we need to avoid extra slab churn (moving metadata triggers compaction).

Kai: prefer embedding in prefix header (already tiny) so eviction doesn't move it; we only update header on mutation. updates are cheap compared to full object writes.

Maya: race: writer arrives after demote consults marker but before remote fetch completes. demote could still return stale value. does that violate our model?

Dani: depends on lease semantics. if writer had a lease and updated marker before responding, demote sees it. if writer hasn't, consistent with causal model — reader may not be able to see in-progress write anyway. we should define exact guarantees: "if writer received ack before reader request, reader must see write". marker must be updated atomically with commit path.

Sam: API sketch that Kai mentioned — small pseudocode:

```
// demote decision API on cache layer
DemoteResult demote(prefix, req_epoch) {
  marker = read_marker(prefix) // returns epoch or 0
  if (marker >= req_epoch) return DemoteResult{action: FETCH_REMOTE, marker_epoch: marker}
  else return DemoteResult{action: SERVE_LOCAL}
}
```

Kai: if marker_epoch >= req_epoch we force fetch_remote; else can serve local (even if value stale older than marker window). marker_epoch comes from last committed mutation.

Maya: test plan: we need a synthetic race harness that can flip eviction at precise point and assert read-after-write invariants. suggest 3 tests: writer-before-evict, writer-during-evict, writer-after-evict with delayed remote apply.

Dani: add telemetry: demote_calls, demote_forced_fetch, demote_miss_after_fetch, marker_mem_bytes. that'll let us tune TTL in prod.

Sam: also think about compaction: when the backend compacts tombstones we should compact marker to zero to avoid forever-pinned prefixes. compaction job needs to clear markers atomically with tombstone purge.

Kai: good call. proposed lifecycle: on mutation commit -> write marker(epoch); on compaction that removes tombstone -> clear marker; eviction may evict value but retain marker until TTL expires or compaction clears it.

Maya: security/privacy: markers must not leak sensitive content. keep them opaque (epoch+crc) only. no keys/ids.

Dani: corner: cross-shard migration where prefix moves — marker must be migrated with prefix metadata. ensure handoff copies marker and its TTL offset so new shard honors same protection window.

evict-bot: RFC link added: https://redwood.internal/rfc/kv-marker-demote (automated: watchers: eng-runtime, eng-platform)

Sam: next steps: draft RFC follow-up with API, storage encoding (8 bytes), compaction integration plan, and test harness. propose canary in dev cluster for 2 weeks with metrics enabled.

Kai: i'll draft RFC today. calling out decisions to make: marker size (8 vs 16), TTL default (30s vs 5m), whether marker update is sync on commit or async.

Maya: +1 to sync on commit for correctness; we can optimize later if perf is bad.

Dani: i'll skecth the race tests and metric dashboard.

Kai: thanks all — small follow-up: please add any gotchas to the RFC PR thread.

Maya: one more: consider a debug flag to surface marker state in tenant-level traces for oncall debugging.

Kai: good idea. i'll include that.

Sam: :thumbsup:
